Before you know what kindness really is you must lose things, feel the future dissolve in a moment like salt in a weakened broth. What you held in your hand, what you counted and carefully saved, all this must go so you know how desolate the landscape can be between the regions of kindness. How you ride and ride thinking the bus will never stop, the passengers eating maize and chicken will stare out the window forever.
Before you learn the tender gravity of kindness, you must travel where the Indian in a white poncho lies dead by the side of the road. You must see how this could be you, how he too was someone who journeyed through the night with plans and the simple breath that kept him alive.
Before you know kindness as the deepest thing inside, you must know sorrow as the other deepest thing. You must wake up with sorrow. You must speak to it till your voice catches the thread of all sorrows and you see the size of the cloth.
Then it is only kindness that makes sense anymore, only kindness that ties your shoes and sends you out into the day to mail letters and     purchase bread, only kindness that raises its head from the crowd of the world to say it is I you have been looking for, and then goes with you every where like a shadow or a friend.
I am not one soul healing alone.  I am a doorway my grandmother walks through.

Caption
find your sanctuaries  we tend to think of a sanctuary as somewhere we have to escape to. somewhere quiet, beautiful, far enough away from everyday life that we can finally exhale.  but finding sanctuary doesn’t require escape, expense, or excess.  a sanctuary is a container. a space that gives you something you need in order to come back to yourself.  and different sanctuaries can give us different things.  a library can be a sanctuary because it gives you somewhere to feed your mind. you can find writers who make you feel less alone, ideas that open something up in you, or words that bring you new perspective.  water can be a sanctuary when you need to clear your energy.  your body can be a sanctuary because it is the one home you always carry with you. a place where you can belong to yourself completely. where you don’t have to perform, prove, or be anything other than who you are.  your rituals can create sanctuary when they connect you to the sacred.  you might have more than one sanctuary. I know I do.  as you keep building your grounding practice this month, find your sanctuaries and practice returning to them. these are the spaces that bring you back - that help you feel more like yourself again.  #wordsforyourjourney #gentlereminders

i often see this in healing sessions: rest starts to feel unsafe long before anyone can explain why.

not because they don't know how to rest. because somewhere along the way, being useful became the thing that kept them safe, loved, or connected — and the body never got the memo that it's allowed to stop.

so even when the mind understands rest is allowed, the system still responds like usefulness is the price of belonging.

swipe through for what that pattern can look like energetically — and what it takes to work with it, not just around it. 🤍

if this feels familiar, book a session with me at the link in my bio.

what if the issue isn’t that you don’t know how to relax, but that (deep down) resting makes you feel unsafe?

I see this pattern often in healing sessions, especially when usefulness has become tied to safety, love, or belonging.

swipe through for what that can look like energetically and if this feels familiar, book a session with me at the link in my bio.

you can still be capable, ambitious, caring, and generous without feeling anxious every time you choose to take a break. 🤍

xx donnie

caption   what’s it like?  this is probably the question I get most often about my shamanic healing sessions, so I wanted to pull back the curtain a little bit.  the way clients describe it is: part conversation, part psychic reading, part coaching - mixed with crystals, drumming, and energy healing. it’s hard to describe exactly, but almost everyone has some version of the same responses:  “I feel so much calmer” “that was not what I expected” “when can I do another”  most clients don’t actually know what they’re looking for when they book. they just know something feels off, stuck, or ready to be cleared.  you don’t need to have the answers or even an inkling of what’s going on. you just need an intention for the session.  my job is to work with the helping spirits to see what’s ready to shift or come to light, and then do whatever is needed to facilitate that transformation.  I offer private and small-group sessions virtually and in person in westport, ct.  dm me to learn more 🤍 xx donnie
